clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old man with sickle cell anemia and prior splenectomy with common ligation of splenic vessels 26 years ago presented with fever and ascites. CT-angiography on admission revealed a giant splenic aneurysm (9.8 cm × 5 cm) located at the site of previous vessel ligation, with a concomitant arteriovenous shunt demonstrated by contrast infusion into an enlarged splenic vein. The aneurysm and AV-shunt were associated with large-volume ascites (4 liters intraoperatively) and hemodynamic complications. The patient underwent open surgical repair via supra-infraumbilical incision 24 hours after admission. Intraoperative findings included a covered rupture of the fragile, hemorrhagic aneurysm embedded in a giant omentum sac. Vascular repair was performed by cross-clamping and ligation of the splenic artery and vein using 4-0 Prolene sutures and Teflon implants. At 6 days postoperatively, the patient developed fever with elevated inflammatory markers, paralytic ileus, and hemorrhagic pancreatitis documented on CT and digital subtraction angiography. Sepsis was successfully treated during a 20-day ICU stay. The patient was discharged in good clinical condition after closure of the abdominal cavity without further complications.

final.final_diagnosis: Giant splenic aneurysm with concomitant arteriovenous shunt, portal hypertension, ascites, paralytic ileus, and peritoneal infection due to hemorrhagic pancreatitis
final.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old man with sickle cell anemia and prior splenectomy with common ligation of splenic vessels 26 years ago presented with fever and ascites. CT-angiography on admission revealed a giant splenic aneurysm (9.8 cm × 5 cm) located at the site of previous vessel ligation, with a concomitant arteriovenous shunt demonstrated by contrast infusion into an enlarged splenic vein. The aneurysm and AV-shunt were associated with large-volume ascites (4 liters intraoperatively) and hemodynamic complications. The patient underwent open surgical repair via supra-infraumbilical incision 24 hours after admission. Intraoperative findings included a covered rupture of the fragile, hemorrhagic aneurysm embedded in a giant omentum sac. Vascular repair was performed by cross-clamping and ligation of the splenic artery and vein using 4-0 Prolene sutures and Teflon implants. At 6 days postoperatively, the patient developed fever with elevated inflammatory markers, paralytic ileus, and hemorrhagic pancreatitis documented on CT and digital subtraction angiography. Sepsis was successfully treated during a 20-day ICU stay. The patient was discharged in good clinical condition after closure of the abdominal cavity without further complications.
